chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the eunuch and the elderly woman: is the women's tawaf obligatory upon them? He said, 'Yes, the tawaf is obligatory upon all of them.'

And whoever forgets the women's tawaf until he returns to his family, then women are not permissible for him until he returns and performs the women's tawaf. If he is unable to return, it is permissible for him to order someone to perform tawaf on his behalf. If he dies and has not performed it, his guardian should perform it on his behalf. That which indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: The women's tawaf (a specific circumambulation in Hajj)
key_terms.يَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ: That which indicates this (introductory phrase for the supporting narration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women's tawaf for eunuchs and elderly women, and what happens if they forget it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that eunuchs and elderly women are fully obligated to perform *tawaf al-nisa'* (the women's circumambulation) to complete their Hajj rites. It establishes a practical legal mechanism for those who forget this rite before departure, allowing for proxy performance or guardianship fulfillment, thereby ensuring the validity of their pilgrimage even in cases of absence or death.
